sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: Comprehensive study of **Mountains, Hills & Glaciers** (पर्वत, पहाड़ियाँ एवं हिमनद) in the context of Indian Physical Geography.
Geological evolution spanning from the **Precambrian Era** (Peninsular block) to the **Tertiary Period** (Himalayas).
Physiographic divisions of India including **Northern Mountains**, **Peninsular Plateaus**, **Western Ghats**, and **Eastern Ghats**.
Essential preparation material for aspirants targeting the **UPSSSC PET** (Preliminary Eligibility Test) examination.
Forms the backbone of Indian climate, river systems, biodiversity, and mineral resources tested in competitive exams.
**Fold Mountains** (Himalayas), **Block Mountains** (Satpura, Vindhya), **Residual Hills** (Aravalli), and major **Glaciers** (Siachen, Gangotri).
High-scoring static GK area involving direct factual questions on **peaks**, **passes**, **ranges**, and **glacier locations**.
Includes highest peaks like **Mount Everest**, **K2 (Godwin-Austen)**, **Kanchenjunga**, and major peninsular peaks like **Anamudi**.

items.title: Classification of Mountains based on Formation
items.content:
• **Fold Mountains:** Formed by the compression of tectonic plates (e.g., **Himalayas**, **Alps**, **Andes**).
• **Block Mountains:** Formed by faulting and displacement of earth's crust, creating **horsts** and **grabens** (e.g., **Satpura**, **Vindhya**, **Black Forest**).
• **Volcanic Mountains:** Formed by the accumulation of volcanic material (e.g., **Mount Kilimanjaro**, **Mount Fuji**).
• **Residual/Relict Mountains:** Formed by the erosion of existing elevated landforms (e.g., **Aravalli**, **Eastern Ghats**, **Nilgiri**).
• **Mnemonic for Mountain Types:** **'F-B-V-R'** -> **F**old, **B**lock, **V**olcanic, **R**esidual (Remember: **F**ast **B**ikes **V**ex **R**iders).

items.title: Himalayan Ranges from North to South
items.content:
• **Trans-Himalayas (Tethys Himalayas):** Northernmost range including **Karakoram**, **Ladakh**, and **Zaskar** ranges.
• **Greater Himalayas (Himadri):** Highest range with an average elevation of **6,000 meters**, containing **Mount Everest**, **Kanchenjunga**, and **Nanga Parbat**.
• **Lesser Himalayas (Himachal):** Middle range with famous hill stations like **Shimla**, **Mussoorie**, **Nainital**, and ranges like **Pir Panjal** and **Dhauladhar**.
• **Outer Himalayas (Shiwaliks):** Southernmost foothill range composed of unconsolidated sediments with longitudinal valleys called **Duns** (Dehradun) and **Duars**.
• **Mnemonic for Himalayan Ranges (North to South):** **'T-G-L-O'** -> **T**rans, **G**reater, **L**esser, **O**uter (Remember: **T**all **G**iants **L**ove **O**ranges).

items.title: Major Glaciers of India
items.content:
• **Siachen Glacier:** Located in the **Karakoram Range**, longest glacier outside the polar regions (~**76 km**).
• **Baltoro Glacier:** Located in the **Karakoram Range**, feeding the **Shigar River**.
• **Gangotri Glacier:** Located in **Uttarakhand** (Garhwal Himalayas), source of the **Bhagirathi River** (Ganga).
• **Yamunotri Glacier:** Located in **Uttarakhand**, source of the **Yamuna River**.
• **Milam & Pindari Glaciers:** Located in **Kumaon Himalayas**, feeding tributaries of the **Sharda River**.
• **Mnemonic for Major Glaciers:** **'S-B-Ga-Ya'** -> **S**iachen, **Baltoro**, **G**angotri, **Y**amunotri (Remember: **S**unny **B**oys **G**et **Y**ellow).

items.title: Peninsular India Mountain Ranges and Hills
items.content:
• **Aravalli Range:** One of the oldest fold mountains, running from **Gujarat to Delhi**, highest peak is **Guru Shikhar** (Mount Abu).
• **Vindhya Range:** Acts as a water divide between **Northern and Southern India**, composed of sedimentary rocks.
• **Satpura Range:** Block mountain range running parallel to Vindhyas, bordered by **Narmada** and **Tapi** rift valleys.
• **Western Ghats (Sahyadri):** Continuous mountain chain parallel to the western coast, highest peak **Anamudi** (Kerala).
• **Eastern Ghats:** Discontinuous, eroded hill ranges along the eastern coast, highest peak **Mahendragiri** (or **Arma Konda**).
• **Mnemonic for Peninsular Ranges (North to South):** **'A-V-S-W-E'** -> **A**ravalli, **V**indhya, **S**atpura, **W**estern Ghats, **E**astern Ghats.

items.title: Highest Peaks in India Sequence
items.content:
• **K2 (Godwin-Austen):** **8,611 meters**, located in the **Karakoram Range** (PoK/Gilgit-Baltistan) — Highest peak in India (disputed territory).
• **Kanchenjunga:** **8,586 meters**, located in **Sikkim** — Highest peak in undisputed Indian territory.
• **Nanda Devi:** **7,816 meters**, located entirely within **Uttarakhand, India**.
• **Kamet:** **7,756 meters**, located in **Uttarakhand**.
• **Saltoro Kangri:** **7,742 meters**, located in the **Karakoram region**.
• **Mnemonic for Indian Peaks:** **'K-K-N-K'** -> **K**2, **K**anchenjunga, **N**anda Devi, **K**amet (Remember: **K**een **K**ids **N**ever **K**it).

items.definition: Remember **K-L-Z** from North to South for Trans-Himalayas: **K**arakoram, **L**adakh, **Z**askar. (Acronym: **K**eep **L**earning **Z**oology).
Remember **A-M-D** from South to North: **A**namudi, **M**esapudi, **D**odabetta. **Anamudi** is the undisputed giant of the south.
Spans from **Palampur (Gujarat)** through **Rajasthan, Haryana**, up to **Raisina Hill (Delhi)** where Rashtrapati Bhavan is situated.
Longitudinal valleys between Lesser Himalayas and Shiwaliks are called **Duns** in the West (Dehradun) and **Duars** in the East.
Ganga starts from **Gangotri** (Bhagirathi), Yamuna from **Yamunotri**, Indus from **Bokharchu** glacier near Mansarovar.
Vindhya range separates North India river systems from South India. Satpura lies south of Narmada and north of Tapi.

items.term: Mistake 1: Highest Peak in India Confusion
items.definition: Students often confuse **K2 (Godwin-Austen)** with **Kanchenjunga**. K2 is the highest peak in India (in PoK/Ladakh), but **Kanchenjunga** is the highest peak in undisputed Indian territory (Sikkim).
Students mistake Aravalli for young fold mountains. Aravalli is actually one of the **oldest fold mountain systems** in the world, currently existing as relict/residual hills.
Many confuse **Dodabetta** (Nilgiri) with **Anamudi** (Anaimalai). **Anamudi** is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and entire South India.
Shiwaliks are the **outermost and youngest** Himalayan range, made of unconsilidated river sediments, not ancient crystalline rocks.
Karakoram range is **NOT** part of the Greater Himalayas; it belongs to the **Trans-Himalayas** (Tethys Himalayas) located further north.
Remember that **Narmada river flows BETWEEN** Vindhya and Satpura ranges in a rift valley, with Vindhyas to the north and Satpuras to the south.
The Himalayas stretch over **2,400 km** from Indus gorge in the west to Brahmaputra gorge in the east in an arc shape.
Himalayas were formed by the collision of the **Indo-Australian Plate** with the **Eurasian Plate**, uplifting the Tethys Sea sediments.
Located north of the Great Himalayas, containing the **Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar, and Kailash** ranges.
Continuous mountain range with permanent snow cover, housing peaks like **Everest, Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Dhaulagiri, and Nanga Parbat**.
Rugged mountain system known for health resorts, tourist spots, and famous ranges like **Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, and Mahabharat**.
Lowest and newest Himalayan foothills with flat-floored structural valleys known as **Duns** (e.g., Dehradun, Kotdwar).
Eastern branch of Himalayas turning southwards through Northeast India, including **Patkai Bum, Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, and Mizo Hills**.
Stable, ancient landmass comprising old fold mountains like **Aravalli, Eastern Ghats, and Western Ghats**.
Steep escarpment parallel to Arabian Sea, acting as a major water divide and hosting rich biodiversity hotspots.
Discontinuous, low-elevation hill ranges dissected by major peninsular rivers like **Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery**.
Himalayan glaciers such as **Siachen, Gangotri, and Zemu** are vital freshwater reservoirs feeding perennial rivers of North India.
Strategic passes like **Zoji La, Shipki La, Nathu La, and Bomdi La** facilitate cross-border trade, military movement, and communication.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks direct factual questions matching mountain peaks with their respective states or mountain ranges. Memorize the top 5 highest peaks in India and their exact locations.
Pay close attention to river origin points associated with glaciers (e.g., Bhagirathi from Gangotri, Alaknanda from Satopanth glacier) as these are standard geography questions in UP exams.

Examinees often trap themselves by confusing 'highest peak in India' (K2, disputed in PoK) with 'highest peak in undisputed Indian territory' (Kanchenjunga in Sikkim). Read question options very carefully.
Do not assume all mountain ranges in India are young fold mountains. Aravalli and Eastern Ghats are ancient relict/residual mountains formed in Precambrian and Archean eras.
Remember the North-to-South ordering of Himalayan subdivisions (Trans -> Greater -> Lesser -> Shiwalik) and East-to-West river divisions (Punjab, Kumaon, Nepal, Assam Himalayas).

keyTakeaways: Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by tectonic plate collision involving the Tethys Sea.
K2 is India's highest peak (in Karakoram), while Kanchenjunga is the highest in undisputed Indian territory.
Aravalli is one of the world's oldest fold mountains, stretching from Gujarat to Delhi.
Western Ghats (Sahyadri) culminate at Anamudi peak in Kerala, the highest point in Peninsular India.
Siachen is the longest glacier in the Karakoram range and outside the polar regions.
Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand is the traditional source of the Bhagirathi branch of the Ganga river.
Major mountain passes like Zoji La, Shipki La, and Nathu La act as crucial gateways across the Himalayan barrier.
